description: NGC 224 is a research-oriented team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We aim to develop an intuitive lunar landing site analysis platform to study sunlight availability and direct-to-Earth communication opportunities near the Moon's south pole. Our interests include astronomy, space science, Python, scientific computing, data analysis, and software development. We welcome curious, collaborative members passionate about research and space exploration.

The platform generates and evaluates candidate site–epoch combinations over a selected lunar region. It provides an interactive polar terrain map, illumination and visibility timelines, candidate rankings, constraint evaluations and reproducible scientific reports. In the Connecting Ridge reference study, LunaScope evaluated nine candidate locations across three landing epochs, producing 27 opportunities: four passed the configured constraints and 23 failed.

details:
Project Details — LunaScope

LunaScope is a scientific lunar south-pole landing-site analysis platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge's Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge. It evaluates how terrain topography, solar illumination and geometric visibility of Earth vary across candidate surface locations and landing epochs.

How it works

The platform integrates NASA's Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) digital elevation model with JPL DE421 planetary ephemerides through the NAIF SPICE toolkit. A terrain-processing engine samples the lunar surface and performs radial horizon ray-tracing to estimate local topographic obstruction. Topocentric geometric calculations evaluate solar and Earth positions relative to each candidate location.

Users can define geographic search regions, landing epochs, surface-stay durations and operational constraints. LunaScope evaluates candidate site–epoch combinations, classifies each as PASS, FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE, and ranks eligible opportunities using configurable multi-criteria utility models. Results are presented through an interactive lunar polar map, candidate analysis panels, illumination timelines, Earth visibility profiles and reproducible reports.

Demonstrated results and benefits

The Connecting Ridge reference study evaluated nine physical candidate locations across three landing epochs, producing 27 site–epoch opportunities. Four opportunities satisfied the configured constraints, while 23 failed. The highest-ranked opportunity achieved a BALANCED utility score of 0.7000.

This approach helps compare locations and landing windows systematically, identify illumination limitations, examine terrain-related horizon obstruction and understand why particular opportunities satisfy or violate selected constraints. It also provides traceable results that can support preliminary mission-planning decisions.

Creativity and intended impact

The central innovation is the integration of spatial terrain evaluation with temporal landing-window analysis. Instead of treating a landing location as a fixed point on a map, LunaScope evaluates the relationship between location, landing epoch and surface-stay duration. This creates a time-aware framework for comparing candidate opportunities.

The platform also emphasizes scientific transparency through data provenance, cryptographic checksums, explainable rankings, explicit failure conditions and distinctions between numerical precision and physical uncertainty.

Its intended impact is to support more informed lunar exploration planning by making complex terrain and illumination analysis accessible through an interactive research environment. The architecture can also be extended to evaluate additional lunar regions, landing epochs and mission constraints.

Technologies and development tools

  • Programming: Python, TypeScript and JavaScript.
  • Backend: FastAPI, Pydantic and NumPy.
  • Astrodynamics: NAIF SPICE, SpiceyPy and JPL DE421.
  • Terrain data: NASA LOLA PDS3 digital elevation model.
  • Frontend: Next.js 15, React 19 and Tailwind CSS.
  • Scientific visualization: Interactive polar stereographic mapping, terrain visualization and temporal data charts.
  • Testing: Pytest, Ruff, TypeScript, ESLint and Playwright.
  • Deployment and packaging: Docker and Docker Compose.
  • Development hardware: Apple Silicon ARM64 environment.

Engineering considerations and limitations

Development considered polar coordinate singularities, anisotropic spatial sampling, DEM coverage, terrain interpolation, celestial disk geometry, temporal sampling, computational resource requirements and reproducibility. Missing terrain coverage is not treated as zero elevation, and results retain their original data and model provenance.

LunaScope is a preliminary scientific trade-study platform, not a landing-safety certification system. Safe landing assessment, rover traversability, power-system feasibility and RF communications link closure remain NOT_EVALUATED. The system does not claim NASA approval or flight certification.
